Publications

Selected research.

Four experiments in measuring change with scattered light.

4 published studies

Optics Letters · 50 (19)2025

How paint dries

Following paint-drying dynamics across spatial and temporal scales, without tracking individual particles.

Read the paperCo-first author
Inside the experiment+

Research question

How can speckle analysis resolve evolving paint-drying dynamics at different spatial and temporal scales?

Method
DDM-based laser speckle analysis
Samples
100 & 200 µm paint layers
Analysis
Time & spatial frequency

My contribution

  • Contributed to differential-dynamic-matrix analysis of laser speckle patterns.
  • Investigated the evolving optical response during paint-layer drying.
  • Compared the dynamics of 100 and 200 µm layers across spatial scales.
Key outcome

DDM-LSA resolved evolving dynamics across spatial scales without direct particle tracking. The 100 µm layer stabilized faster, while the 200 µm layer retained longer-lived activity.

The reported comparison concerns the paint layers and acquisition conditions shown in the publication.
Speckle pattern analysis using differential dynamic matrix

Measurement · Volume 2442025

Reading a vibrating battery

Reading the response of vibrating batteries through secondary laser speckle.

Read the paperFirst author
Inside the experiment+

Research question

Can vibration-induced changes in a secondary speckle pattern distinguish battery states without direct electrical contact?

Illumination
632.8 nm He–Ne
Acquisition
140 frames per second
Excitation
Controlled vibration

My contribution

  • Investigated secondary-speckle responses under controlled battery vibration.
  • Analyzed correlation-derived pattern displacement and its frequency response.
  • Examined full-versus-empty discrimination and changes during NiMH discharge.
Key outcome

Distinct speckle responses separated the tested full and empty batteries, while signal metrics also followed NiMH discharge.

Results concern the tested batteries and vibration conditions; this study does not establish a universal battery-health calibration.
Remote battery evaluation by secondary speckle patterns

Scientific Reports · 16, 208062026

Watching powder lose moisture

An optical signature of moisture-driven change in cornstarch powder.

Read the paperCo-first author
Inside the experiment+

Research question

Can dynamic speckle fluctuations provide a non-contact optical signature of moisture-driven changes in powder?

Illumination
632 nm He–Ne
Acquisition
10 frames per second
Sample
Cornstarch powder

My contribution

  • Contributed to non-contact laser-speckle monitoring of powder drying.
  • Analyzed time-history speckle patterns during a humidity transition.
  • Compared optical trends with independent surface-profilometry measurements.
Key outcome

The optical trends agreed with surface profilometry, supporting speckle analysis as a non-invasive way to follow the measured drying process.

The study presents an optical signature of the drying process; it does not claim direct, absolute moisture-content measurement.
Remote monitoring of powder dehumidification by speckle pattern analysis

Measurement · Volume 2192023

Sensing current from a distance

Using current-dependent speckle activity for non-contact electrical sensing.

Read the paperCo-first author
Inside the experiment+

Research question

Can optical speckle activity reveal DC current in an insulated wire without direct electrical contact?

Illumination
632.8 nm He–Ne
Acquisition
25 frames per second
Measurement
Non-contact DC-current sensing

My contribution

  • Contributed to camera-based laser speckle measurements from insulated wires.
  • Investigated current-dependent speckle activity using temporal analysis.
  • Examined calibration responses across conductor materials and wire diameters.
Key outcome

Current-dependent speckle activity enabled calibration-based estimation across the wire materials and diameters tested.

The reported results concern the tested insulated wires, conductor materials, and wire diameters.
Laser speckle analysis for remote detection of electric current flowing in wires

Background

About me.

My work moves between the optical bench and the camera image. I build experiments around small changes in scattered light, then analyze the images to learn what changed in the sample.
